extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents), respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and OED/USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 imposing suspension, stay, probation, and related procedural and publication obligations on a registered patent practitioner based on reciprocal state-bar discipline. The document specifies grounds for discipline, timelines, enforcement procedures, reinstatement rules, and notice/publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for suspension under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 (ethical violation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), suspension from practice before the USPTO may be ordered for violation of the ethical standards set out in 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b), via 37 C.F.R. §10.23(a)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline can be imposed based on a state authority's suspension for ethical misconduct; the Director may suspend a practitioner when the OED Director files a complaint for reciprocal discipline under §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely file international patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's suspension was predicated upon 'failure to timely file three international patent applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late or omitted filings of international patent applications may constitute ethical misconduct supporting state and USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cure fee deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the predicate misconduct: 'to cure fee deficiencies regarding one of the three applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to address or cure required fee deficiencies on client matters is actionable misconduct and can support suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to communicate accurate information to the client
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicate misconduct included 'to communicate accurate information to the client regarding the patent applications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing inaccurate or misleading information to clients about their patent matters is an ethical violation relevant to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to maintain file materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicate misconduct included 'to maintain file materials that Respondent should have maintained.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper or inadequate maintenance of client files is a ground for professional discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's duty to file a timely response to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order directed Respondent to file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely, substantive response within the specified period is required to contest reciprocal-discipline allegations; failure to respond is treated as a basis for finding no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of no genuine issue of material fact under §11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file the required response, the Director may determine that 'there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)' and that suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-response permits the Director to accept the OED Director's allegations and impose reciprocal discipline without further factual hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of suspension, stay, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO for twenty-four (24) months beginning thirty (30) days after the date of the Final Order; after serving the initial two months of the suspension, the final twenty-two (22) months are stayed and Respondent is immediately eligible to request reinstatement; Respondent shall serve a twenty-two (22) month probationary period commencing three months after the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order defines precise start dates, initial active suspension period, conditions for staying the remainder, and the separate probation period timing and interaction with reinstatement eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent 'shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 while serving the suspension imposed herein.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners suspended under USPTO rules must follow §11.58 requirements (e.g., notification to clients, file handling) while their suspension is in effect; this obligation also applies if suspended during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Gazette notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette identifying the respondent, registration number, suspension term, and the misconduct basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO discipline includes public notice obligations—publication in the Official Gazette and dissemination of the final order content summarizing the misconduct and regulatory bases (35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to USPTO employees, agencies, and state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of this Final Order to (1) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (2) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; (3) appropriate authorities of any State in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary orders require intra- and inter-governmental notification so other actors are informed of the practitioner's status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probationary noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with any terms of the Final Order during the 22-month probationary period, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent at the last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause is the initial enforcement step during probation; it affords the respondent a short period to contest alleged noncompliance before further action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate suspension process upon continued noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 15‑day response period, if the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response, and evidence supporting the opinion for imposition of an immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued noncompliance during probation can lead to expedited imposition of an immediate suspension based on the compiled materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing for review does not stay suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event Respondent seeks a review of the USPTO Director's decision to suspend, 'any such review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the immediate suspension of Respondent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial review of the suspension decision does not automatically stay enforcement of the suspension imposed by the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED obligations if suspension occurs during probation (37 C.F.R. §11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Respondent is suspended during any portion of the 22-month probationary period pursuant to the Final Order, the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED must follow §11.59 procedures (e.g., publication and notification) when suspensions are imposed during probationary periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limit on number of suspensions under the Final Order during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall limit the number of times during his probation that Respondent may be suspended pursuant to this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated suspensions may be imposed under the order if the respondent repeatedly fails to comply with its terms during probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek further discipline for the same misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent for the same misconduct that causes a suspension pursuant to this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order does not preclude additional disciplinary proceedings or sanctions for the same acts of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement application requirements under 37 C.F.R. §11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, after completing the initial two months of the 24-month suspension, may apply for reinstatement to practice before the Office upon filing a petition for reinstatement that 'complies fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.60.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is conditional on meeting the procedural and substantive requirements of §11.60 (e.g., proof of fitness, compliance with order terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record as aggravating factor or rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including this Final Order, 'be considered when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct ... and/or in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor ... and/or to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past disciplinary findings are admissible and may worsen future sanctions or be used to counter respondent's claims in subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent 'bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order specifies that each party is responsible for its own costs related to the proceeding and the order's implementation.
